title: Fiber hearing correspondence: privacy and presentation
decision_question: Retain full resident correspondence, authorize a redacted derivative/summary, or leave this material held?

options.consequence: Owner accepts the privacy exposure; any implementation follows a separate visible review stage.
Authorize a separate redaction/editorial stage while preserving original provenance and distinguishing derivatives.
Preserve the existing original and evidence without further archive or content action.

why_owner_judgment_required: The preserved correspondence contains resident communications and complaints. Choosing full originals, redaction or a summary determines privacy exposure and editorial presentation; source recovery cannot make that choice.

title: ART advocacy records: contributed-source editorial policy
decision_question: Admit these attributed contributed advocacy records within an ART historical evidence package, or exclude/hold them under the official-record editorial policy?

options.consequence: Owner permits nongovernment primary evidence with explicit authorship and viewpoint labels; no claim of official findings or approved minutes.
Record an owner editorial exclusion; existing historical bytes are preserved and any visible removal needs manual review.
No new visible action while editorial disposition remains open.

why_owner_judgment_required: These are identified advocacy/commentary and a participant meeting account, already preserved as contributed originals. Their nongovernment authorship is not disputed. The genuine choice is whether ABQInfo admits this attributed advocacy evidence, rather than representing it as an official government finding.

title: DPM historical proposals: retention and presentation
decision_question: Preserve these as explicitly historical proposals within a DPM series, or limit the public historical package to adopted standards and minutes?

options.consequence: Retain as proposals only, with draft dates and adopted-record relationships; never label them current or enacted.
Apply an editorial exclusion of these proposals while preserving dated research and any existing original bytes.
No new archives or content for this family pending owner editorial choice.

why_owner_judgment_required: Draft labels and Chapter 7 proposed status are established. No owner is asked to determine adoption. The editorial choice is whether substantive pre-adoption proposals belong in a clearly labeled historical proposal series alongside adopted standards, given the already preserved sibling draft.

title: Wireless review checklist: borderline public-information value
decision_question: Does this code-interpreting staff checklist merit retention as a historical regulatory aid, or exclusion with routine application paperwork?

options.consequence: Default: prefer final wireless regulations and application standards over an internal routing checklist.
Owner admits its distinct interpretation value; subsequent archival and visible editorial review remain required.

why_owner_judgment_required: The ten-page City checklist interprets a named Albuquerque zoning-code section but is also an internal applicant-routing form. Its substantive local regulatory content is credible; the usefulness of a separate retained record is genuinely close.
